title: GTA 6 Is Going To Be Huge. So Why Is Take-Two’s Stock Having Such A Bad Year?
description: Take-Two owns one of the largest entertainment franchises out there in Grand Theft Auto. The newest entry, GTA 6, launches this November. There is enormous hype for the new game, which is expected to sell millions of copies at launch and break records. In short, it's expected to be a once-in-a-decade (if not ever) kind of title. The game is also coming to market with a lot of positive sentiment and excitement. If you're a Take-Two shareholder, however, the past year has been a big bummer. Take-Two's share price has slid about 15% so far this year and is down about the same over the past year, meaning anyone who invested in the past year has lost money (at least on paper; gains or losses are not realized until positions are sold) in the run-up to GTA 6's release in November. What's going on here? There are plenty of factors involved in what could be driving Take-Two's stock price down, and plenty of reasons that this could ultimately just be a short-term blip. Zooming out First, it's important to zoom out. In the past five years, Take-Two's stock price is up 39%. That is short of the growth of the S&P 500 (+73% over the past five years), but it's still very solid for a single stock in a competitive field. Going back even further shows even greater gains for anyone who bought and held Take-Two. For example, after Strauss Zelnick and his team at ZelnickMedia successfully completed a hostile takeover of Take-Two in 2007, the stock exploded in price. Take-Two shares were trading at around $20 back then. Today, Take-Two trades at around $215. When GTA 5 launched in 2013, Take-Two was trading at about $18. Clearly, the stock did gangbusters since then, continuing to surge over the years as Take-Two expanded its portfolio to include numerous other heavy hitters while increasing profitability with microtransactions and recurring revenue. Lucia and Jason in GTA 6 So why is Take-Two stock down this year? Take-Two, along with other game companies like Roblox, got hammered in…

title: Nintendo Finally Adds Some Life To The Switch 2
description: Both of Nintendo's Switch consoles have been cursed with deafening silence in their menus and eShops. But the latest version 23.0.0 update for the Switch 2 at least injects a little bit of personality and nostalgia into one of the platform's menus, bringing back music for the Mii Maker. When you create a Mii in the Switch 2's system settings, the familiar Mii Channel music from the Wii now plays in the background. A music settings button on the top left also lets you change the track to the 3DS or Wii U Mii Maker music (the tracks are generically named "Track 1," Track 2," and "Track 3"). Certain Nintendo fans feel that the company's platforms have lost some of their soul with the lack of music and visual themes, so this update, as small as it is, can be taken as a nice gesture. Unfortunately, both Switch platforms are still without any eShop background music or visual themes. Nintendo omitted these menu elements for the first Switch to save processing power and allow users to quickly navigate the UI to start their games. At the very least, it seems like the Switch 2 has some extra juice to accommodate some Mii music. The Switch 2 firmware update allows users to share their Miis through QR codes. While Miis might not be as big a deal for Nintendo as they were in the Mii days, the cartoony avatars are still very much a part of modern games like Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream and the upcoming Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. Version 23.0.0 also adds a quick setting for the Switch 2's handheld boost mode and support for variable refresh rate. Finally, the patch includes "stability improvements," as per tradition.

title: Here’s How Wanted Levels And Crime Work In GTA 6
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is overhauling the Wanted and police response systems in an interesting way. If you've played Grand Theft Auto games before, you'll know that if you do something illegal, the police will show up. You'll get a wanted level represented by stars--the more stars you have, the more aggressive the police, or even the military, will be. In order to get out of the situation, you evade the police. You'll see them on the map, so it's easy to lay low for a minute and get them off your back. That is not the case in GTA 6. In the extended gameplay trailer, we did get a look at how some of this works, but more details have surfaced through some exclusive coverage. The first thing we noticed was the return of the six-star wanted level. This was missing in GTA 5, but in older games if you got six stars it would call in the military. Looking at the return of the six stars, it could happen that the military could also get involved. GTA 6 sees the return of six-star wanted levels. In GTA 6, instead of the police searching your specific area for a short time, they'll cast a much wider net. That means that wherever you go in Leonida, the police will be on alert and looking for you. There's far more than just the star system in GTA 6. Some of the icons underneath the stars tell a story, too. These symbols tell you exactly what the police are looking for when you commit a crime. An icon of a CCTV camera means you've been spotted on one, and you'll have to destroy the evidence to get rid of that. A symbol with two characters means the police have seen Jason and Lucia together, meaning you should split up to avoid being recognized. The hanger symbol means the police recognize your clothing so you should change. It seems like you can store clothes in your car, so having outfits at hand will be useful as long as nobody sees you changing. The face icon means they recognize your facial features, so you probably should have been wearing a mask. To get rid of this icon, wear a…

title: Marvel’s Wolverine Isn’t Cutting It? Try These Games Instead
description: Marvel's Wolverine reviews have officially gone live, and while the overall consensus isn't terrible, it's not another critical hit for Spider-Man studio Insomniac Games. On GameSpot's sister site Metacritic, Marvel's Wolverine currently has a metascore of 77 from 102 reviews, with many reviewers pointing out that it doesn't live up to the standard of superhero games that Insomniac has defined with its Spider-Man adventures. "At best, it’s a fun but forgettable experience that’ll entertain you for a few hours. At worst, it shows that just because you can make really good superhero games with one character, that doesn’t mean you can make really good super hero games with any character," editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's Marvel's Wolverine review. Those opinions might leave some people feeling disappointed, but that doesn't mean that there aren't other options to consider. Is it possible to play as Wolverine in a good game or to check out a release that channels the spirit of Marvel's favorite Canadian? Absolutely, and we've gathered a few recommendations below for you to check out. X-Men Origins: Wolverine Starting with the obvious, Raven Software's official tie-in for the infamously bad X-Men Origins: Wolverine movie is a rare example of a game being better than the movie it's based on--much, much better. It's short and sweet, but it's an action-packed journey that covers the movie and new sequences made especially for the game. The combat still holds up, and Wolverine's pounce attack is an evergreen combat mechanic that still feels as exciting to pull off today as it was when the game first came out in 2009. The only problem here? You're not going to find it for sale online, as Activision delisted this Wolverine game in 2014. It's also not backwards compatible with Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S, so your best bet is to dust off an old console or rummage through a bargain bin to see if you can find a physical PC copy of it. title: Wardogs’ Massive Start On Steam Undercut By Brutal Server Queues [Update]
description: Update: A hotfix has now been released for Wardogs that targets the ongoing server issues. If you're logged in and stuck in a queue, you'll need to close the game to download the update, which will then send you back into a queue once you log in again. Players will be allowed into the game in "controlled batches," the size of which were not specified, and might portend continued queues for the time being. More players will be let in as the issues are resolved, but no specific timetable is provided for how long that could take. Alongside the long queues, the patch targets issues with joining servers and an issue causing players to be kicked from matches. "We will be actively monitoring the ongoing situation post hotfix and will be working through the night to see this resolved," the developer wrote in a post on Steam. "We apologize for the inconvenience this has caused." Original story: A big new military FPS, Wardogs (not to be confused with the 2016 Jonah Hill/Miles Teller crime-comedy War Dogs) launched today in early access on Steam, and it's off to a hot start. The shooter reached 300,000 peak concurrent users on Steam right out of the gate and the $40 game is currently Steam's No. 1 best-seller. Pretty impressive for a game that the developer told you not to buy. Given the flood of players, developer Bulkhead instituted a server queue system, and this quickly became something of a meme on social media. Players shared screenshots of the queue and their place in it--some people reported having more than 300,000 people in line in front of them. Yeesh. Bulkhead responded to the brutal queueing situation, saying it was partly due to the developer being "rate limited." The company said it was working with Valve to resolve this limit and get an increase in line with "larger titles." Things got worse, temporarily albeit, for some, as Bulkhead made the decision to kick everyone from the queue as a fix that, in theory, would help more players get into the game faster.…

title: Nintendo Adds VRR To Docked Nintendo Switch 2 Play In The Most Annoying Way
description: More than a year after its launch, the Nintendo Switch 2 finally has support for variable refresh rate when docked and connected to a TV--feature which has always been possible in portable mode. Headlining the Switch 2 version 23.0.0 update, which is out now, VRR can now be enabled in the console's settings menu for docked play. It will require a separate update for the dock itself too, which will be applied the next time you dock the console. Also included in the update is a system-transfer feature, which might come in handy a few weeks ahead of the release of the special edition Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Switch 2. Curiously, the patch notes indicate that VRR will only engage with compatible games, suggesting that developers will need to update their games to make it available. Currently, Nintendo Switch 2 Welcome Tour is the only game that supports docked VRR, with the game's VRR demo now unlocked in docked play. It's a strange requirement for a hardware-level feature, and might make its adoption either slow or inconsistent. Variable refresh rate allows a compatible display to match the frame rate of the game being played, within a specific frame-rate window. It's immensely useful for games with variable performance and unlocked frame rates, like Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, as it can alleviate distracting screen tearing and stuttering. It has been supported by the Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 since their respective launches, and has been a staple in many TVs for the past couple of years. It's been a busy week for Nintendo, with a Direct for The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary that was mostly focused on the remake for Ocarina of Time. A day later, Nintendo hosted a more traditional Direct, with reveals for Metroid Ravenous, Kirby and the World Beyond, and several Nintendo Switch 2 editions of popular Switch titles.

title: Amazon Luna Introduces Its Most Ambitious Feature Yet In A Rough Month For Cloud Gaming
description: As part of its September update, Amazon Luna introduced a Remote Play feature that lets people play games together, even if they aren't in the same room. If you haven't heard of it, Luna is Amazon's cloud gaming service for Prime subscribers that lets them access and play a catalog of games without the need for a console or PC. While some Luna games have had multiplayer features, you previously needed to be in the same room with others to play those titles. Remote Play intends to solve that by letting Amazon Prime and Luna Premium subscribers invite up to seven others into their sessions. These other players won't need an Amazon Prime subscription to use Remote Play, although they will need to use Luna's website or TV app. Of course, you'll now be relying on the smooth internet connections of even more players to comfortably use Remote Play, but the same goes for similar features on PS5 or Nintendo Switch 2. The logo for Amazon Luna To promote Remote Play, Amazon also released two new multiplayer-focused games today. One is a digital version of the board game King of Tokyo, while the other is It's Quiz Time: Guinness World Records, a competitive trivia game. Later in September, it will add the motion-controlled Bowling Mayhem and Pictionary-like Cranium Planet to the game catalog. Star Wars Outlaws and Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora were also added to the Luna Standard game lineup today, although those are single-player games. This Remote Play update is one of the most substantial additions to Amazon Luna in some time, and it arrives in a month that hasn't been so great for cloud gaming. Last week, Xbox confirmed it will limit Game Pass Ultimate subscribers to just 15 hours of cloud gaming a month and make them pay extra for anything beyond that. As Amazon Luna is included with Prime and just got this Remote Play feature, that makes it a little bit more alluring as a cloud gaming option.

title: GTA 6 Trailer Drove 100,000 Netflix Sign-Ups In The US Alone In One Day, Analyst Claims
description: Netflix and Rockstar Games worked together on the recent 26-minute GTA 6 Extended Look trailer, and it seemingly paid off in multiple ways for the streaming company. After Netflix's own data showed that the Extended Look was incredibly popular with viewers, it's now been reported that the Extended Look drove more than 100,000 people to sign up to Netflix that day in the US alone. This is according to Ampere Analysis, which added that the Extended Look was the third-biggest Netflix event in 2026 for new subscriber sign-ups. The two bigger events were the final season of Stranger Things and the Ronda Rousey vs. Gina Carano MMA fight, Ampere said. Ampere went on to say more than 5% of US Netflix members who hadn't watched any content on the service in the previous 30 days before the Extended Look came back to watch it "before anything else." Ampere said this "reactivation rate" was higher than any other show or movie on Netflix during that 30-day period. "More than 100,000 sign-ups from a six-hour exclusive window shows the pulling power of a major gaming event. For Netflix, it also offers a way to compete with YouTube for gamer attention and to bring lapsed viewers back to the platform. For Rockstar, Netflix opens GTA 6 up to audiences beyond the franchise’s traditional core," Ampere's Louise Wooldridge said. The Extended Look was indeed just that--offering the deepest look yet at Rockstar's big new game. The video showed off a variety of gameplay and cutscenes, and teased out some of the new features people can expect. For more, check out GameSpot's breakdown video above to get up to speed with everything we learned about GTA 6 in the new footage. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it appears people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

title: PlayStation Dropping Physint Has Fans Trying To Figure Out What Went Wrong
description: A decade ago, at its PlayStation E3 press conference, Sony introduced veteran game designer Hideo Kojima in grand fashion to show off the first trailer for Death Stranding. It's now 2026, and that partnership appears to have fizzled out, as Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor, Physint, has found a new home at Xbox after Sony dropped it. The Metal Gear Solid creator has also confirmed that he received notice from the company that it intended to cancel Phsyint, leading to several months in which the project was shopped around before Microsoft stepped in to sign a publishing deal. It's yet another baffling decision made by Sony as it continues to set a new speedrunning record for jettisoning goodwill, and naturally, the Internet has a thing or two to say about its divorce from Kojima--including how his studio, Kojima Productions, is situated directly across the road from Sony. You can't make this stuff up! Physint is the second game from Kojima Productions to be made in partnership with Xbox--the first is his upcoming horror game OD--but don't expect to see it for a long time. While the game is a return to his Metal Gear roots with its focus on stealth and espionage, Kojima is also aiming for it blur the lines between movies and video games. Back when the project was still being supported by Sony, Kojima mentioned that it was still several years away from being released, and that timetable may have slipped further after the Sony drama.
